entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Hon'Ble Smt Justice Lalitha Kanneganti
 Criminal Petition No.4529 of 2020
Order:

-
This Criminal Petition is filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short 'Cr.P.C.') to quash the proceedings in C.C.No.251 of 2019 on the file of learned Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Addanki, Prakasam District registered for the offences punishable under Sections 188 and 273 the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short "I.P.C.") and Sections 58, 59 and 63 of the Food Safety Standards Act (for short 'FSS Act').
2.

entities.text: Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Addanki, Prakasam District
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The petitioners before this Court are accused Nos.1 to 4 in the above said C.C.No.251 of 2019.

3. The brief facts of the case are that on 30.01.2019 on credible information that A-1 was selling banned tobacco products i.e. Miraz, Blue Bull, Vimal, Nawab, Khaleja packets to the public at his shop, Head Constable of Martur Police Station went there, caught hold of A-1 and seized tobacco products.
On enquiry, A-1 confessed that A-2 to A-4 supplied tobacco products to him and he in turn is selling the same to the public at higher rates.
Basing on the said statement, the present crime was registered.
4. Heard Sri D.Kasi Rao, learned counsel for the petitioners and learned Public Prosecutor for the State.

5. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that neither of the offences registered under the above sections are applicable to the case on hand as tobacco does not fall under the category of 'food'
and the police have no power to register a case under the above sections except by the designated Food Safety Officer, who is competent to investigate and file charge sheet in view of the rules laid down in Sections 41 and 42 of the FSS Act.
6.

Learned Counsel submits that the composite High Court in similar circumstances passed common order dated 27.08.2018 in Criminal Petition No.3731 of 2018 and batch wherein it was held that the investigation agency will not have jurisdiction to proceed against the petitioners therein and accordingly F.I.Rs. and C.Cs. were quashed.

7. Learned counsel also placed reliance on the common order dated 18.12.2019 passed by a Coordinate Bench of this Court in Criminal Petition Nos.5421 of 2019 and batch, wherein it was held that 'tobacco' does not fall within the definition of 'food' as specified under Section 3(i)(j) of the FSS Act.
In view of the same, he urged to quash the proceedings in the above C.C.No.251 of 2019.

9. In the light of the aforementioned order, this criminal petition is allowed and the proceedings against the petitioners herein in respect of C.C.No.251 of 2019 on the file of learned Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Addanki, Prakasam District are hereby quashed.
